headline: THE UNBEATEN FALL. THE WINLESS RISE.
lead: Amberwood, the perfect season and the winless season checked out on the same receipt. Sahit handed Roshik his first loss while collecting his first win, Abhiram exploded for 176.66, and the playoff picture rearranged itself like a group chat after someone mentions dues. Buckle up: the top five still qualify by record, but the sixth ticket belongs to points, not vibes.
playoff: If the regular season ended after Week 8, the five record berths would belong to Pranav J (7–1, 1,162.08 points), Roshik (7–1, 1,108.42), Anudeep (6–2, 1,116.42), Pranav P (5–3, 1,098.28) and Abhiram (5–3, 1,097.92). This is a snapshot, not a champagne reservation.

Pranav P and Abhiram are separated by 0.36 points. That is not a cushion; that is a rounding error with playoff aspirations. Ankith is also 5–3 but trails Abhiram by 21.72 points in the record tiebreaker. Their Week 9 meeting is a direct fight for positioning.

The sixth berth goes to the highest-scoring team outside the top five. Right now that is Taaha: 1,129.36 points at 2–6, 53.16 ahead of Ankith’s 1,076.20. Taaha is running a championship-caliber offense with a win column that looks like a typo. The wildcard pool changes whenever the top five changes.
toilet: The bottom two seeds get first-round byes in the toilet bowl. In the last-place survival bracket, win and you are safe from finishing last. There is also a tournament for the toilet-bowl winner, with the first pick on the line. That is a real prize: an elite player can turn one miserable season into a very loud draft-night comeback.

After Week 8, Sahit is 1–7; Taaha, Sahil and Gary & Naveen are 2–6. By the current record-and-points ordering, Sahit and Gary & Naveen occupy the bottom two spots, but this is only a snapshot and the seeding can change. Sahit just beat the previously unbeaten leader, so nobody should be treating a matchup with him like a complimentary bye.

recaps.title: Ankith vs Pranav P
paragraphs: Ankith takes the 33.40-point win and joins the crowded 5–3 neighborhood. Pranav P still sits just ahead of Abhiram on points, but this was not the week to request a velvet rope. The bank collected a win and left its opponent checking the balance.
Ja’Marr Chase supplied 33.10 and Braelon Allen added 25.30; Pranav P got 24.90 from Chuba Hubbard.

recaps.title: Abhishek vs Aditya
paragraphs: Abhishek wins by 26.48 and both teams leave at 3–5. Aditya’s 67.58 was the lowest score on the card. His lineup did not so much crash the party as send an email saying it might stop by.
Rashee Rice led Abhishek with 18.30 and Chase Brown added 16.10. James Cook led Aditya with 18.10.

recaps.title: Abhiram vs Sahil
paragraphs: Abhiram drops a league-high 176.66 and wins by 66.46, taking a top-five record berth on the current snapshot. Sahil scored 110.20 and still lost by enough to qualify as a public service announcement.
Tee Higgins piled up 39.50, Harold Fannin Jr. 25.40 and Bucky Irving 23.00. Jaylen Warren led Sahil with 22.30.

recaps.title: Sahit vs Roshik
paragraphs: Sahit gets his first win at the expense of previously unbeaten Roshik, 149.06–111.10. Roshik is 7–1 and remains in excellent shape, but the undefeated parade has been rerouted directly through the toilet-bowl district. Sahit picked a spectacular time to stop being polite.
Bhayshul Tuten delivered 31.90 and Michael Wilson 28.80 for Sahit. Brock Bowers’ 28.20 and Josh Jacobs’ 23.20 could not keep Roshik perfect.

recaps.title: Pranav J vs Gary & Naveen
paragraphs: Pranav J rolls to 175.12 and a 61.36-point win, moving to 7–1 and first on the points tiebreaker. Gary and Naveen had two managers, but neither could locate an answer for that avalanche.
Tony Pollard scored 30.20 and Puka Nacua 25.00. On Monday, D’Andre Swift added 27.90. Josh Allen contributed 26.56 for Gary & Naveen.

recaps.title: Anudeep vs Taaha
paragraphs: Anudeep takes it by 24.48 and improves to 6–2. Taaha falls to 2–6 despite 1,129.36 points on the season, currently enough for the points wildcard. The man can score; apparently winning is a premium add-on.
Joe Burrow led the way with 41.48, Jahmyr Gibbs had 26.80 and Matthew Golden 20.90. Jaxon Smith-Njigba gave Taaha 26.30.

mickey: Aditya takes the ears for the week’s lowest total, 67.58. Even a winless team beat the league leader while his lineup posted a number that needs a permission slip to ride the playoff roller coaster. The good news: next week’s scoreboard starts at zero.

rankings.blurb: 7–1 and first on points. The crown fits; now keep it away from Taaha’s points machine.
7–1 after the first loss. One bad Sunday does not erase seven wins, but Sahit did leave a note on the throne.
6–2 and another comfortable win. Quietly building a résumé while everyone else fights over the font.
5–3 and fourth on the current tiebreaker. A 0.36-point edge is a spectacularly thin security blanket.
5–3 and fresh off 176.66. His next opponent is Ankith, who would very much like to repossess that playoff spot.
5–3 and outside the top five for now. The Week 9 showdown with Abhiram is not one to sleep through.
2–6, but 1,129.36 points currently earns the wildcard. The scoreboard loves him; the schedule has other plans.
3–5 after the week’s lowest score. A bounce-back is required, preferably with all starters participating.
3–5 and a win is a win. The style points committee is still reviewing the 94.06.
2–6 after meeting Abhiram’s avalanche. The wildcard is a points chase, and every point still matters.
2–6 and currently in the bottom-two snapshot. Two minds, one mission: escape the cellar.
1–7 after ambushing the previously unbeaten leader. Last in record, first in proving the league can still get weird.

previews.title: Pranav P vs Aditya
previews.blurb: Pranav P defends his razor-thin place in the top five; Aditya needs a response after 67.58. The bar for improvement is reachable without a ladder.

previews.title: Ankith vs Abhiram
previews.blurb: Both are 5–3 and Abhiram currently holds the final record berth by 21.72 points. Direct playoff leverage and no shortage of receipts.

previews.title: Abhishek vs Sahit
previews.blurb: Abhishek looks to build on a win; Sahit just took down the unbeaten leader. Do not mistake 1–7 for a free square.

previews.title: Sahil vs Gary & Naveen
previews.blurb: Both sit 2–6. Every win matters in the race away from the bottom, and nobody wants to audition for the wrong side of the toilet bowl.

previews.title: Anudeep vs Roshik
previews.blurb: A 6–2 contender meets the 7–1 former unbeaten. Roshik has a chance to bounce back; Anudeep has a chance to make that first loss look like a trend.

previews.title: Taaha vs Pranav J
previews.blurb: The current points-wildcard leader faces the standings leader. Taaha’s points deserve a winning record; Pranav J is under no obligation to provide one.
